key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: The OR join condition forces a nested-loop join instead of a hash join; rewriting as a UNION ALL of two separate equi-joins (one on PULocationID, one on DOLocationID) followed by aggregation would enable hash joins and reduce comparisons to ~1M.

value.sql: SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z_pu ON z_pu.LocationID = t.PULocationID JOIN ops.zones z_do ON z_do.LocationID = t.DOLocationID CROSS JOIN UNNEST([z_pu.Borough, z_do.Borough]) AS z(Borough) GROUP BY z.Borough ORDER BY z.Borough
value.change_summary: Rewritten OR join as double equi-join to zones for PULocationID and DOLocationID, then unnest boroughs to preserve per-trip contribution to both boroughs, enabling hash joins.
value.risk_notes: Assumes zones.LocationID is unique (verified). If a trip has same PULocationID and DOLocationID, it will contribute two counts to that borough, matching original OR join semantics.
